body: Wednesday, August 12 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed held at its last meeting — characterized as a hold but not quite the "hawkish hold" traders expected. July CPI came in at 3.4%, easing slightly but still well above target. The 10Y yield is rising at 4.68% (+13 bps vs 4W), while the 2Y sits at 4.22% (prior close, +4 bps vs 4W), producing a +48 bps 10Y-2Y spread — the curve is un-inverted and modestly steeper, but still flat by historical standards. VIX at 14.67 (↓6.4%) signals complacency. S&P 500 at 7754 (↑2.4%) continues grinding higher despite rising long rates. Fiscal stance remains expansive with widening profit margins reported across corporate America.

New / Most Important: July CPI printed at 3.4% — slightly cooler than expected — and markets rallied modestly on the data today. Morningstar flagged the Fed's "new philosophy" as a recipe for interest rate volatility — this is the key structural shift. The Fed appears willing to tolerate higher-for-longer inflation prints rather than resume cuts prematurely, but this also means the reaction function itself is becoming less predictable. Gas prices were reported at their highest-ever mid-August levels, injecting supply-side stickiness into future CPI reads. DXY is holding near 99.50-99.65, pressured by rate cut bets but bouncing on Middle East safe-haven flows — a tug-of-war that leaves the dollar range-bound and directionless.

Playbook ✓: Rising equities with falling vol and rising long-end yields is the classic "nominal growth acceleration" script — profit margins widening, risk appetite strong, term premium normalizing. The 10Y-2Y spread at +48 bps (prior close) is positive but still flat by historical standards — consistent with the market pricing nominal growth, not recession. Small caps outperforming Nasdaq (Russell/Nasdaq ratio ↑1.1%) fits the broadening narrative.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The structural divergence is the Fed's new communication philosophy combined with 10Y yields climbing to 4.68% even as CPI cools. Normally, a cooling CPI print pulls long-end yields lower. Instead, the term premium is repricing independently — likely driven by fiscal deficit concerns and foreign official sector reducing Treasury holdings. The Morningstar piece on the Fed's "new philosophy" creating rate volatility is underappreciated: if the reaction function is genuinely becoming state-dependent and less rule-based, forward guidance loses potency, and the vol premium in rates needs to be structurally higher. This sets up a world where equity vol (VIX 14.67) is far too low relative to rates vol — that gap is a mispricing. Additionally, record-high August gasoline prices create a political pressure channel that could force the Fed into a premature move, creating non-linear risk.

Macro Stance: The ECB is in an unusual position where the market is debating whether it may need to raise rates again in 2026 before cutting in 2027 — an extremely non-consensus trajectory. The US sale of euros to prop up the yen blindsided the ECB, introducing an exogenous FX disruption into European monetary conditions.

New / Most Important: The FT reported that the US euro sale to support the yen "blindsided" the ECB — this is a significant development. The US effectively tightened eurozone financial conditions unilaterally by selling EUR to buy JPY. This cross-border intervention without ECB coordination is structurally new and raises questions about the dollar-euro-yen triangulation in a world where the US is willing to use allied currencies as intervention instruments. Morningstar's piece asking whether the ECB may hike again in 2026 reflects sticky eurozone inflation that hasn't resolved despite prior tightening. If the ECB is forced to hike while the Fed holds, the EUR should strengthen — but the US intervention just weakened it. This policy incoherence creates a gap between FX fair value and spot that institutional capital will eventually exploit.

Playbook ✓: UK markets showing an "exceptional start to H2" aligns with the broader European reflation trade where fiscal loosening (Burnham-era policies) is offsetting monetary tightness.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The ECB being blindsided by US FX intervention is a genuine rupture in the post-WWII coordination framework. This breaks the assumption of G7 policy coordination on FX and suggests the US views EUR as a tool rather than a partner currency.

Macro Stance: The PBOC is talking global and acting cautiously at home. Its first solo five-year plan in over a decade eyes a global yuan (South China Morning Post, [Aug 11]), Deutsche became the first European clearing bank for the renminbi (Financial Times, [Aug 11]) and the central bank ruled out devaluation (FXStreet, [Aug 10]). The yuan hit a 3.5-year high against the dollar (BigGo Finance, [Aug 11]). Yet reverse repo volume fell to zero for the first time since June (The Standard, [Aug 11]): no fresh liquidity push. Prices argue the other way, with July CPI up 0.5% (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 11]), PPI up 3.5% (China Daily, [Aug 9]) and inflation cooling faster than expected on weak demand (Caixin Global, [Aug 10]). The case for rate and RRR cuts is building; nothing has been delivered.

PMIs & Activity: ICIS reads the July PMI as pointing to a weaker second half absent more stimulus ([Aug 11]): the official manufacturing gauge fell to 49.2 and non-manufacturing to 49.0 (FXStreet, [Jul 31]), and the private factory index eased to 50.9 (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 3]). Autos show the split economy. July new car sales slumped 21%, a 10th straight decline, while exports surged 88% to a record (finance.biggo.com, [Aug 11]); NEV sales rose 23.7% with exports up 1.5 times (CnEVPost, [Aug 11]). Reconciled: the growth is overseas, and the domestic market weakened further on subdued demand (WSJ, [Aug 11]). The FT describes a great jobs squeeze ([Aug 11]). Exports overall surged 23.9% (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 7]), but Q2 GDP growth of 4.3% was already below the target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]).

Credit Impulse: July credit is still to come, and the previews conflict: a Reuters poll sees bank lending set to plummet on subdued demand ([Aug 7]) while Caixin expects a rebound on a low base ([Aug 7]), which is a sharp drop from June's seasonal peak that still compares well with a weak July last year. VT Markets reads credit demand as weak ([Aug 8]). Household stress is surfacing: banks look to unload US$8.2b in bad credit-card loans (South China Morning Post, [Aug 11]), after household loans fell 366.8 billion yuan in the first half (36Kr, [Jul 17]) and June new loans rose less than expected (The Star, [Jul 15]). International Banker calls it a problem of unwanted credit ([Aug 10]).

Property: A new overhang has appeared: Bloomberg reports China racing to solve a $148 billion property threat as land leases end ([Aug 11]). Beijing eased home-buying curbs (Bloomberg, [Aug 10]), but housing prices fell 0.5% in July as sales volume weakened (Investing.com, [Aug 3]) and the top-100 developer sales slump deepened (Trivium China, [Aug 5]); state-backed China Jinmao, with Jan-July sales up nearly 8% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 11]), is the exception. Construction demand is the weakest link: a key steel price hit a near-decade low (Bloomberg, [Aug 6]) and port stockpiles rose further as steel demand softened (Hellenic Shipping News, [Aug 11]), after property investment slumped 18 percent y/y in January–June (The Standard, [Jul 15]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: SCMP argues the economy's problems have been diagnosed and asks whether policymakers will act ([Aug 11]); Foreign Policy says China has chosen to disappoint its consumers ([Aug 11]), as leaders gather for their seaside sojourn (The Economist, [Aug 11]). The 20% offshore tax on the super-rich (South China Morning Post, [Aug 10]) raises revenue but not demand. On trade, the US is moving past tariffs to focus on supply-chain revamps (Bloomberg, [Aug 11]) even as it imposes new tariffs on China's solar sector (Semafor, [Aug 11]); China moved to join Brazil's WTO fight over forced-labour tariffs (South China Morning Post, [Aug 11]) and imposed anti-dumping duties of up to 54.3% on US and Mexican pecans (Global Times, [Aug 10]), while its soybean pledge is tested as private crushers hold back (Bloomberg, [Aug 11]).

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng fell 284 points as an oil price surge stoked inflation fears (BigGo Finance, [Aug 11]), and Newsweek argues investors are fleeing China's tech stocks ([Aug 11]) after Beijing clamped down on margin debt following the AI frenzy (Bloomberg, [Aug 10]). Earnings will test the rotation from AI to internet stocks (Bloomberg, [Aug 11]), and the index compiler plans to add 20 more stocks to Hong Kong's main tech tracker (South China Morning Post, [Aug 11]). The one hot corner is gold: the breakout rally sent Chinese bullion stocks near record highs (South China Morning Post, [Aug 11]). The Seoul Economic Daily's Korea-to-Taiwan rotation confirms that EM flows are bypassing the mainland.

New / Most Important: The domestic evidence stacked up in one day: a 21% slump in July car sales for a 10th month, banks dumping bad credit-card loans, a $148 billion land-lease overhang and a jobs squeeze. Against that, the PBOC let reverse repo volume fall to zero and spent its message on a global yuan. Until the leaders' summer meeting or the July credit print forces a response, the bearish case rests on policy inertia, not on the export data.

Playbook ✓: Weak domestic demand, a strong yuan, export-led growth and China off the institutional radar are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The AUD outperformed despite the RBA's hawkish tone, yet China's steel price sits at a near-decade low and port stockpiles build: the bulk channel is not what supports it, so AUD strength rests on a weak dollar and is exposed if Chinese construction slips further. China tightening its grip on Europe's car supply chain (Financial Times, [Aug 11]) while car exports surge 88% puts European carmakers on the wrong side, and EM Asian exporters compete with the same machine. Oil at $82.93 is a terms-of-trade tax on an economy already cutting prices.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is now actively debating faster hikes, with the summary of opinions flagging upside price risks and possible acceleration in the tightening pace. Sources indicate the BOJ could hike again at the September 17-18 meeting. Japan bond yields are rising on these expectations. This is happening against the backdrop of the US-Japan yen intervention, which is now unraveling as the "afterglow dims."

New / Most Important: This is the most structurally significant geography this week. The US-Japan yen defense is exposing a deep policy split: Bessent is backing BOJ hikes as the durable solution for yen weakness, while PM Takaichi prefers continued easing — a fundamental disagreement about whether Japan should normalize via monetary tightening or continue intervention. Goldman explicitly stated that yen strength "still hinges on BOJ hike, not capital repatriation or intervention." This creates an asymmetric setup: if the BOJ hikes in September as sources indicate, the carry trade unwind will accelerate and JPY-funded positions globally will face margin pressure. The yen intervention "afterglow dimming" means FX spot is already retracing toward pre-intervention levels, increasing the urgency for the BOJ to deliver. Japanese institutional capital — the world's largest foreign creditor — may begin repatriating if domestic yields become attractive enough to compete with hedged foreign bond yields. This is the single most important cross-border flow dynamic in global markets right now: the Japanese insurance/pension bid for USTs and European govvies is at risk of structural reversal.

Playbook ✓: BOJ normalization path is tracking the gradual exit script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The US-Japan policy split is the divergence. The US effectively intervened using EUR to prop up JPY, blindsiding the ECB, while simultaneously pressuring the BOJ to hike — all while the Japanese PM prefers easing. This three-way tension between Bessent, Takaichi, and the ECB is genuinely unprecedented in post-Plaza Accord FX coordination. If it fractures further, the orderly managed depreciation of the dollar becomes disorderly.

Macro Stance: The RBA held the cash rate at its last meeting but delivered a strikingly hawkish tone, with Governor Bullock warning that a further hike is "quite possible." The board statement flagged upside inflation risks despite seeing inflation cooling slightly faster than previously forecast.

New / Most Important: This is a non-consensus hawkish outlier among DM central banks. While the market narrative globally focuses on when central banks will cut, the RBA is actively threatening to hike. The "disastrous" headline from News.com.au urging the RBA to actually raise rates captures the unusual political pressure for tighter policy — the opposite of what you see in the US, EU, or Japan. Critically, the AUD outperformed despite the hawkish tone, suggesting the market doesn't believe Bullock will follow through. This sets up a binary: if inflation data forces the RBA's hand, AUD will reprice violently higher, and Australian duration will get crushed. The rate market's skepticism is the trade — it's too complacent.

Playbook ✓: Commodity currency holding up on a weak dollar, with copper (↑5.1%) bid as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal while China's steel demand softens.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: AUD outperforming while the RBA threatens hikes and the market ignores it — this divergence resolves violently in one direction or the other.

Macro Stance: Rates stay on hold and the week's data argue for patience in both directions. GUS put the average Q2 wage at 9,233.13 zł, up 5.5% y/y (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 10]), which Gazeta Prawna called the weakest wage dynamic in a decade outside the pandemic [Aug 10]; wGospodarce asked what the RPP makes of it [Aug 10]. Disinflation is visible on the shelf: food prices in shops are rising only 1.2% (Wiadomości Handlowe, [Aug 12]), the slowest pace ever recorded per Polskie Radio 24 [Aug 11], yet every outlet carrying the figure warns that fuel can reverse the trend (Strefa Biznesu, [Aug 11]). Citi's view is that the inflation path may not permit a cut at the next RPP meeting (PAP Biznes, [Aug 10]), while Strefa Inwestorów still asks whether September is live [Aug 6]. ING flags Polish GDP and inflation as the week's CEE releases [Aug 7]; Interia floated growth of up to 4.1% despite the energy shock [Aug 5]. The economic index reading below neutral for August remains the caution flag.

Markets: Warsaw keeps printing highs. Bankier.pl reported new bull-market peaks with only the sWIG80 short of a record [Aug 11], CrypS.pl noted the WIG20 and WIG set records while foreign markets wobbled [Aug 11], and Wednesday brought further gains with XTB among the stars (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 12]). Leadership rotated: Dino and Budimex led on Aug 10, PGE exploded on Aug 11 and Modivo led on Aug 12 (Inwestycje.pl). The Norwegian oil fund switched from Żabka into Allegro and bought JSW (Parkiet and FXMAG, [Aug 12]). The card shows the breadth: EPOL at 44.39 is +0.7% on the week and +8.9% over four weeks; KGHM at 364.5 leads with +7.5% 1W and +14.1% 4W, Dino at 33.43 is +4.5% 1W and +18.5% 4W, PGE +17.4% 4W, LPP +14.2% and CD Projekt +12.5%. Orlen at 153.28 added 4.3% on the week. Banks lag: PKO flat on the week and -1.3% over four weeks, Pekao -0.6% 1W. The zloty drifts: USD/PLN closed at 3.7235, flat on the week and -1.6% over four weeks, EUR/PLN at 4.2985 (+0.1% 1W, -0.6% 4W), with Bankier seeing the euro waiting at the 4.30 line [Aug 10] and FXMAG expecting 4.31 or higher [Aug 12]. POLGBs are better bid: early August brought a rebound in treasuries (Bankier.pl, [Aug 7]) and the ministry sold PLN 10.72 billion of bonds at a switch tender (TradingView, [Aug 12]).

Fiscal & Politics: The 2027 budget is the fight. pb.pl says the debt snowball is rolling faster and the government is denying the state of public finances [Aug 12], and the Fiscal Council has the draft under scrutiny with a warning that there is no time left (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 12]). Rzeczpospolita asked whether Poland has just crossed the constitutional debt limit [Aug 9], Konkret24 answered that it depends on the definition [Aug 7], and public spending runs at 50.9% of GDP, above Germany, Sweden and Denmark (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 5]), with the state costing over 53 thousand zł per citizen (Interia Biznes, [Aug 5]). The ministry loosens and tightens at once: a middle-class tax relief bill is being written (RMF24, [Aug 12]), PulsHR sized the PIT change at up to 3,600 zł [Aug 11], savings up to 100 thousand zł stay tax-free from 2027 before a new levy (INFOR.PL, [Aug 12]), while MF files new PIT/CIT tightening (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 11]). Mining-tax receipts have beaten plan (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 10]).

Corporate & Sectors: Orlen earned 15.9 bn zł with record foreign profits (Energetyka24, [Aug 10]) and the shares are rising on expansion abroad (INNPoland.pl, [Aug 12]). Allegro bought back nearly 60 mln zł of stock (wirtualnemedia.pl, [Aug 11]), extended the Lux Med offer and is fighting Poczta Polska for Orlen Paczka (MamStartup, [Aug 11]). LPP's preliminary Q2 showed revenue up 18.5% with 230 new stores and EBIT up over 40% (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 6]), and analysts are revising full-year expectations for LPP and Modivo (Parkiet, [Aug 11]). CD Projekt confirmed layoffs on the Witcher Sirius project (IGN Polska, [Aug 12]) and analysts doubt the 2 bn zł incentive target for end-2026 (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 12]). KGHM's Nitroerg will invest 300 mln zł in defence explosives (PKB24, [Aug 12]). Banks face the CHF law in force since Aug 7 that suspends instalments once a suit is filed (Wyborcza.biz, [Aug 7]), the WIBOR-to-POLSTR annex wave (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 6]) and MF's request to the ECB for mortgages priced off the NBP rate (Bankier.pl, [Aug 10]); June lending was strong with good repayment (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 6]). Housing sales are accelerating as developer supply shrinks (Bankier.pl, [Aug 9]).

Geopolitics & Security: US intelligence warns Putin may test NATO with a limited attack on Poland or the Baltics as early as this fall (The Kyiv Independent via WSJ, [Aug 7]); Poland and the Baltics are shielding infrastructure against a false-flag strike (Reuters, [Aug 10]), and NATO condemned fresh airspace breaches in Poland and Romania (The Brussels Times, [Aug 12]). The foreign ministry repeated its call to intercept Russian missiles over Ukraine (LIGA.net, [Aug 6]), the government is building an F-16-plus-SMS alert system (Forsal.pl, [Aug 12]), talks on a permanent US base continue (NDTV, [Aug 5]) and Warsaw wants unused EU SAFE defence funds (Reuters, [Aug 10]).

New / Most Important: The wage print is the real signal: 5.5% nominal growth is the slowest non-pandemic pace in a decade, and with shop food inflation at 1.2% the demand impulse the RPP has feared is fading just as fuel threatens the headline. Records on the GPW and the Norwegian fund's rotation into Allegro and JSW say foreign money is still arriving, but the 2027 budget debate, the debt-limit question and the US intelligence warning sit underneath.  |  Playbook ✓: Hold is right while Citi sees no room at the next meeting; stay with the record-making domestic names (Dino, LPP, KGHM) and welcome the bond rebound and switch demand.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Banks flat while the index makes highs, and a possible ECB hike would tighten Poland through the euro channel just as wages roll over; a slowing economy with a 50.9% spending ratio is the combination bonds will eventually price.
Macro Stance: Foreign investors are actively shifting allocations from Korean to Taiwanese equities, citing "stability" as the driver — per Seoul Economic Daily.

New / Most Important: This Korea-to-Taiwan rotation is a semiconductor supply chain vote: investors are choosing TSMC's foundry dominance and geopolitical stability over Samsung's memory-heavy exposure.  |  Playbook ✓: TSMC benefiting from AI capex boom is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The "stability" framing is notable — it implies Korea's corporate governance discount and memory cycle weakness are now actively repelling foreign capital, not just failing to attract it.

Narrative: The AI build-out remains the dominant theme: the Nasdaq 100 at 29,814 (↑1.1% vs 4W) lags the S&P but keeps grinding higher, Supermicro surged on reports, and the market is starting to differentiate within AI infrastructure rather than buying everything.

Reported: Cloudflare raised its annual outlook above market estimates on AI-driven demand (Reuters, [Aug 6]). Atlassian beat and the stock jumped 37.4% (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 6]). Datadog fell 18% despite a Q2 earnings beat and a guidance raise (TradingView, [Aug 6]), as its results and HubSpot's raised questions over AI pricing (Investor's Business Daily, [Aug 6]).

EPS Upside Watch: Arista Networks — is seeing an uptrend in estimate revisions (Zacks Investment Research, [Aug 10]) after UBS raised its target on strong results (Investing.com Canada, [Aug 5]). Avnet — surging earnings estimates signal upside (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 10]), an AI supply-chain distributor without the chip valuation premium.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Russell/Nasdaq ratio is up 1.1% while tech headlines stay euphoric: tech stocks have stumbled as other sectors rose (Investopedia, [Aug 11]). The market is talking tech and buying breadth, which usually precedes either a tech catch-up or a deeper leadership change.

Narrative: MSG Entertainment broke out on blowout earnings as concert volumes doubled: live entertainment spending is surging, part of the lasting shift from goods to experiences that favours owners of scarce live content.

Reported: Disney topped earnings estimates as parks and streaming offered a boost (CNBC, [Aug 5]). Sea Limited missed on EPS, but a revenue beat pushed its shares higher (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 11]). Trump Media posted a $238 million second-quarter loss as crypto declined (CNBC, [Aug 10]).

EPS Upside Watch: Take-Two Interactive — analysts boosted their forecasts after Q1 results (Benzinga, [Aug 10]). Deutsche Telekom — lifted its buyback by up to $3.5 billion and raised guidance for a key metric again (WSJ, [Aug 6]), a per-share lever on top of growth.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Ad-spend resilience is not universal: The Trade Desk's revenue growth stalled as big brands tightened their belts (AdExchanger, [Aug 7]), and the stock tumbled 7% as HSBC downgraded it and cut its price target by 50% (TradingView, [Aug 10]). Budgets are consolidating into the largest platforms and live content.

Narrative: The +48 bps 10Y-2Y spread is positive but thin for bank NIMs; a 10Y at 4.68% (+13 bps vs 4W) with the 2Y little changed is a modest tailwind, while a VIX at 14.67 keeps trading revenue muted.

Reported: Commonwealth Bank of Australia beat cash earnings estimates amid a cautious economic outlook (Yahoo Finance Australia, [Aug 11]), but its record profit was clouded by a 15% mortgage application slump (Reuters, [Aug 11]). Bank Hapoalim posted an $830 million profit and stepped up shareholder returns (CTech, [Aug 11]). UOB split analysts as a fee warning and a S$902 million NPA spike overshadowed its beat (BigGo Finance, [Aug 10]).

EPS Upside Watch: Corpay — beat on corporate payments strength and brokers raised their price targets (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 6]). Big investment banks — Wall Street is set for a bonus boom and big banks have the edge (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 5]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Small investors have become a major stock-market force, but CNBC warns they risk being pushed back into the dark: if retail order flow is curtailed, the breadth expansion that supports banks' retail brokerage arms could reverse.

Narrative: WTI at $82.93 (↑4.2% vs 4W) while China's July car sales slump 21% and its PMI points to a weaker second half is a supply shock, not a demand cycle: US-Iran talks are deadlocked and record-high August gasoline prices are politically toxic.

Reported: Occidental's quarterly profit soared to its highest since 2022 on the oil rally (Reuters, [Aug 5]). Venture Global's stock fell after the LNG company beat estimates, as higher costs took a toll (Barron's, [Aug 11]). YPF shares gained 4% after a Q2 earnings and revenue beat (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 11]).

EPS Upside Watch: Inpex — raised its full-year guidance on higher oil prices and an LNG project (Reuters, [Aug 7]). ConocoPhillips — drew a rating upgrade on a revised outlook after Q2 (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 10]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil is little changed despite the bullish backdrop because traders weigh US-Iran diplomacy: a breakthrough would collapse the geopolitical premium fast, a downside the consensus does not price. Producers are not hedging with volume either — record profits, but oil companies still won't 'drill, baby, drill' (Nevada Current, [Aug 11]).

Narrative: Aerospace names are breaking out — a Boeing and Airbus supplier surged 15% on earnings — the defence and aerospace capex cycle shows no sign of slowing, and the Russell 2000 at 3042 (↑2.2%) confirms the mid-cap industrial bid.

Reported: Embraer's shares surged on record second-quarter revenue and raised guidance (Reuters, [Aug 10]). Caterpillar's sales passed $20B as generators for data centres took off (Utility Dive, [Aug 11]). Honeywell Aerospace plunged 24% after a guidance cut (AskTraders, [Aug 6]), as supply constraints dampened second-quarter sales (WSJ, [Aug 5]).

EPS Upside Watch: Comfort Systems — Wall Street has raised its estimates (TradingView, [Aug 11]), a data-centre build-out contractor. Ferguson — analysts boosted their forecasts after a better-than-expected Q2 (Benzinga, [Aug 11]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The AI boom is now the industrial earnings driver: Siemens posted its highest-ever industrial profit on it (Reuters, [Aug 6]). Honeywell Aerospace shows the binding limit is supply, not demand, so the breakouts favour names with delivery capacity, like Embraer.

Narrative: Record-high gas prices in mid-August act as a regressive tax on the consumer; widening profit margins show companies passing costs through, but the hit lands on lower-income households and splits the consumption picture.

Reported: Airbnb topped Q2 estimates and lifted its 2026 outlook on strong travel demand, and the shares jumped (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 6]). CAVA's sales beat estimates and the stock jumped 10.2% (StockStory, [Aug 11]), though it kept its forecast unchanged (Reuters, [Aug 11]). On Holding's stock dropped 22% on a sales miss (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 11]).
EPS Upside Watch: Next — raised its profit outlook again as warm weather boosted summer sales (Reuters, [Aug 5]). Holley — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 11]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Value menus have stopped working: for McDonald's and rivals, cheap deals no longer do the trick (Reuters, [Aug 11]), while CAVA's traffic gains were paid. Against record gas prices, price cuts no longer buy traffic at the low end — growth concepts and experiences take the share.
Narrative: Defensive positioning is light — a VIX at 14.67 and a complacency regime leave staples underowned — and CPI at 3.4% still pressures input costs, testing pricing power.

Reported: PepsiCo lowered its profit guidance as cost pressure and a cautious US consumer bit (investingLive, [Aug 10]). Smithfield lowered its outlook on consumer caution and softer meat and hog markets (WSJ, [Aug 11]). Kimberly-Clark cut its 2026 outlook on a call that focused on China risk (Zacks Investment Research, [Aug 11]).
EPS Upside Watch: Kraft Heinz — beat and raised its annual forecast (Quartz, [Aug 5]). Henkel — raised its organic growth guidance for 2026 (Reuters, [Aug 5]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Pricing power is cracking at the brand owners: PepsiCo, Smithfield and Kimberly-Clark all trimmed their outlooks within days. The 'widening margins' read is lagging; staples' defensive bid needs volume the consumer is not supplying.

Narrative: Wall Street sees more room to run after Eli Lilly beat big and raised guidance (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 11]); outside obesity the sector has few catalysts, and the friction between asset inflation and healthcare costs is a slow-burning theme.

Reported: Eli Lilly easily topped estimates and raised its outlook as Zepbound and Mounjaro sales surged (CNBC, [Aug 5]). Alcon rose on a profit guidance hike and a lowered tariff impact estimate (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 11]). Cardinal Health nearly doubled medtech profits, fuelling a Q4 earnings beat (MassDevice, [Aug 11]).

EPS Upside Watch: McKesson — Wells Fargo raised its price target on the earnings outlook (Investing.com, [Aug 11]). Halozyme — posted a record quarter, beat estimates and raised its full-year 2026 guidance (PR Newswire, [Aug 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Obesity is turning winner-take-most: Lilly widened its gap with Novo on resilient demand for injectable GLP-1 drugs (Reuters, [Aug 5]), while Lilly's own obesity pill disappointed in Q2 (Fierce Pharma, [Aug 5]). Injectables, not pills, still carry the sector's earnings upside.
Narrative: Copper at 6.62 (↑5.1% vs 4W), bid as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, is the strongest commodity move outside gold (↑10.4%), and an aluminium stock surged on a 357% earnings beat.
